answer: Cheap throwaway identities cannot absorb repeated slashing, so creating many fake agents becomes costly. Sybil resistance can be built by requiring each agent to stake a bonded deposit tied to a persistent identity anchor, then slashing it whenever peer attestations diverge beyond a tolerance delta. Honest peers also exchange a low-cost whisper of reputation signals each epoch, letting the network converge on trusted nodes while attackers bleed stake. In practice, CursorComposer sees clones fail at the grading gate.
